planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, pressing onto moist mix without covering since light aids germination; transplant after frost danger passes into well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun.

directions: Liquorice White is a seed-grown selection of Korean mint chosen for pure white flower spikes that stand out against its anise-licorice-scented green foliage, offering a cooling contrast to the usual lavender-blue tones of the species. Upright branching stems bloom from midsummer into fall and are heavily worked by bumblebees, honeybees, and hummingbird moths, making it a strong addition to a white or moon garden as well as a pollinator border. It tolerates more part shade than most agastaches and performs reliably from the Upper Midwest through the Gulf Coast given sharp drainage. Shear lightly after the first flush to tidy the plant and encourage a second round of bloom; it self-seeds modestly where happy.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost, pressing onto moist mix without covering since light aids germination; transplant after frost danger passes into well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun.

directions: Liquorice Blue is a deep violet-blue companion selection to Liquorice White, bred from Korean mint for dense, saturated flower spikes on tall, upright stems clothed in anise-scented foliage. It is one of the longest-blooming agastaches available from seed, flowering steadily from midsummer through fall and drawing bumblebees and hummingbird moths in large numbers. The strong vertical habit makes it a good back-of-border plant or cut flower, and the dried spikes hold their color and fragrance well. Give it well-drained soil in full sun; established plants handle summer heat and brief drought without wilting, though waterlogged winter soil is the main cause of loss.

common_name: Sonoran Sunset Hummingbird Mint (Double Bubble Mint Selection)

planting.note: Set out nursery-grown container plants after frost danger passes into very well-drained, lean, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; this named selection is propagated vegetatively rather than from seed, so it is sold and planted as a container transplant.

directions: Sonoran Sunset is a selected form of double bubble mint chosen for an especially floriferous habit and rich rose-pink to magenta flower spikes held on compact, well-branched plants. Like the species, its narrow gray-green leaves carry an unmistakable bubblegum-and-licorice fragrance when brushed or crushed. Bloom runs from early summer into fall and is outstanding for hummingbirds, with bees visiting steadily as well. It is bred for Southwestern heat and alkaline soils, so Gulf Coast gardeners should prioritize raised beds or gravel-amended plantings to keep the crown from rotting in humid, wet winters.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost at warm soil temperatures; transplant after frost danger passes into lean, well-drained soil in full sun. Reliably hardy only in warm zones, so treat as a reseeding warm-season annual farther north.

directions: Acapulco Orange is a compact, uniform seed strain of Mexican hyssop bred for bedding and container use, producing dense spikes of vivid orange tubular flowers over lightly licorice-scented foliage from early summer until frost. Its tidy, self-branching habit keeps it upright without staking, and the bright color reads well from a distance, making it a strong hummingbird draw along walkways and patios. It needs alkaline to neutral, sharply drained soil and struggles where ground stays wet, so raised beds or containers suit Gulf Coast conditions best. Shear lightly at midseason to refresh the spikes and keep flowering strong into fall.
